full_judgment:
2. Plaintiff firm M/s Ram Ratan Das Banarashi Lal filed the aforesaid suit on the allegations, inter alia, that on 5.1.1955 defendant No. 2 seized 12 items of goods from his godown at Kushtia Bazar as per detention memo Ext. 1 on suspicion; that at the time of the seizure as well as before the Collector of Central Excise and Land Customs sufficient proof as to their lawful possession by the plaintiff was placed but they totally ignored them; that out of the 12 items of goods seized 4 items namely 120 bags of bidi leaves, 9 bags of Dhup, 34. bags of catcchu and 958 bundles of coir strings were confiscated by order dated 3.9.1955 of the Collector of Central Excise and Land Customs, Chittagong Ext. 2(b); that the plaintiff purchased 120 bags of bidi leaves on 25.11.54 vide Ext. 21(1) from Nabi Hossain who auction purchased the same on 10.11.54 from Railway Lost Property office Santahar; that the plaintiff purchased 5 bags of Dhup from M/s SN Gupta & Co. on 23.2.57 vide Ext. 19. 11 bags of Dhup from M/s. TP Khetwat on 10.12.57 vide Ext. 19(a), 6 bags of Dhup from BB Shaha & Brothers on 10.8.59 BS-26.11.52 vide Ext 31 and 3 bags in police auction Kushtia on 24.10.54 Ext. 34 & 34(a) and after gradual sales there remained 9 bags which were seized: that the plaintiff purchased 15 bags of catechu on 12.5.54 Ext. 19(b), 25 bags of catecheu on 11.7.54 Ext. 19(c), 8 bags catechu on 19.7.54 Ext. 19(g), 44 bags of catechu on. 7.11.54 Ext. 19(e), 11 bags of catechu on 11.11.54 Ext. 19(d), and 24 bags of catechu on 18.11.54 Ext. 19(f) from their commission agent Jain company who purchased the same from various importers such as Dada Limited & others and out of the same 24 bags were damaged due to sinking of boat, 69 bags sold and remaining 34 bags were seized; that the plaintiff purchased 55 bundles of coir strings each from Biswanath Singh on 17.5.54 Ext. 21, Tarapada Saha on 17.5.54 Ext. 21(a), Banat All on 18.5.54 Ext. 21(b), Bishnu Ghosh on 18.5.54 Ext. 21(c) and 50 bundles each from Aditya Kumar on 20.5.54 Ext. 21(d). Fanindra Nath Roy on 20.5.54 Ext. 21(c) Atair Ram on 20.5.54 Ext. 21(f) and Harendra Nath Saha on 20.5.54 Ext. 21(g), 450 bundles from Maliram Agarwalla on 1.7.54 Ext. 25 and 475 bundles from Nabi Hossain on 25.11.54 Ext. 21(h); that the aforesaid 8 persons imported 420 bundles without import permit in contravention of import restriction and got the same released on payment of penalty, etc. as per order dated' 10.3.54 Ext. 4(a), that Maliram Agarwalla imported 450 bundles without import permit in contravention of import restriction and got the, same released on payment of penalty, etc. as per order dated 26.10.53 Ext. 24; that Nabi Hossain auction purchased 475 bundles from Railway Lost Property office, Santahar on 5.11.54, 8.11.54 and 10.11.54 Ext. 25(a) to 25(c); that the aforesaid persons brought the said goods through Railway; that out of 1345 bundles 387 bundles were sold and remaining 958 bundles were seized; that the said goods purchased by the plaintiff were either duty paid or duty free and plaintiff's possession was neither illegal nor unauthorized as the same were imported either under valid licence from whom plaintiff purchased the same or plaintiff purchased the same from auction purchasers; that plaintiff's possession of the said goods did not come within the mischief of section 167(81) of the Sea Customs Act 1878 read with section 3(3) of the Import Export (Control) Act 1950; that plaintiff filed an appeal before the Central Board of Revenue against Collector's order of confiscation of the said goods and the said appeal was wrongly rejected on 25.6.56 Ext. 2 and thereafter plaintiff filed a revision before the central government and by order dated 11.10.56 said revision was also rejected vide Ext. 2(a). 

 Defendant-appellants contested the suit by filing a joint written statement denying material allegations and stating, inter alia, that the suit was not maintainable; that civil Court had no jurisdiction to entertain or try the suit as the question whether the seized goods were smuggled goods and liable to confiscation was within the exclusive jurisdiction of the custom authorities and under sections 188 and 191 of the Sea Customs Act such decision was final; that the disputed goods were not duty paid goods but smuggled and Nabi Hossain did not purchase 120 bags of bidi leaves in Railway auction nor the plaintiff purchased the same from Nabi Hossain on 25.11.54 and plaintiff could not produce any receipt at the time of seizure of the same nor to any custom authority thereafter till after 4 or 5 months and subsequently manufactured the same in collusion with Nabi Hossain; that at time of seizure of Dhup plaintiff could not produce any receipt, stock book or account book and the same were smuggled goods; that seized catechu were smuggled goods and were not purchased through M/s. Jain Company and no receipt or voucher or account could be produced by the plaintiff for the same; that seized coir strings were also smuggled goods and the same were neither imported nor purchased as alleged and the plaintiff could not produce any receipt, voucher or account books at the time of seizure and receipts and other documents alleged to have been produced before the customs authorities were fabricated and manufactured in collusion with those persons 4/5 months after the seizure; that neither at the time of the seizure nor before the Collector plaintiff could place satisfactory proof of lawful possession of the disputed seized goods; that after careful consideration of everything placed Collector released 8 items of seized goods and confiscated items of the disputed seized goods as the plaintiff could not satisfactorily account for their lawful possession; that the order of confiscation was lawful and plaintiffs suit was liable to be dismissed with cost. 

 4. Mr. MA Aziz, learned Advocate appearing with Mr. M Rezaul Karim Advocate, submitted that in view of the evidence on record and position of law as to burden of proof in the matter order of confiscation of the disputed goods was without jurisdiction and as such court below had jurisdiction to try the suit and rightly decreed the same. 

 10. The court below held that "Section 177A of the Sea Customs Act is not applicable in the present case and the onus of proof lies on the defendants to prove that the goods in question were smuggled goods." Section 177A and item 81 of section 167 of the Sea Customs, Act were inserted by Ordinance No. HI of 1954 on 18th December, 1954 only 18 days before the seizure of the suit goods. Court below in this respect relied on the decision in the case of Sardar Ali and others Vs. 1. The Collector of Customs Karachi 2. The Federation of Pakistan reported in PLD 1957 (Karachi), 111. In that case certain goods were seized by the Customs authorities on the 18th December, 1954 on the very day of promulgation of the said Ordinance No. III of 1954 incorporating section 177A in the Sea Customs Act 1878 placing burden of proof "upon the person in whose possession goods were found or from whose premises goods were recovered or the person claiming the ownership of the goods". On an appeal by the government against that decision Supreme Court of Pakistan in the case of Federation of Pakistan and another Vs. Sardar Ali and others reported in 11 DLR (SC) 59 held as follows: 

 "The position then appears to be that item 81 of section 167 creates a new substantive offence in respect of certain class of goods which was not contemplated by item 8. By virtue of the new section of 177A, if any question arises in respect of such goods, inter alia, as to whether duty has been paid or secured in respect of them or whether they had been lawfully imported, the burden of proof would lie upon the person in whose possession the goods were found or from whose premises they were recovered or who claimed their ownership."
